facts.text: South Richmond Hill’s first train stop, the Richmond Hill station on the Montauk Line, opened in the 1870s and helped spark the neighborhood’s growth.
Jahn’s Ice Cream Parlor, a 1930s‑era shop, sits among Victorian‑style homes that give South Richmond Hill a nostalgic, time‑travel feel.
The area is celebrated for its deep roots in tradition and history, earning it the nickname “New York’s best kept secret.”.
A 1929 movie theater, RKO Keith’s Richmond Hill, now operates as a bingo hall, preserving a piece of the neighborhood’s entertainment past.
Renowned Beat writer Jack Kerouac lived in South Richmond Hill from 1950 to 1955, adding literary flair to the community’s legacy.
Two Queens Public Library branches—Richmond Hill on Hillside Avenue and Lefferts on Lefferts Boulevard—serve the neighborhood’s residents.
